title: Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites
summary: Amalickiah took those who went with him into the land of Nephi among the Lamanites and stirred the Lamanites to anger against the people of Nephi. The Lamanite king sent a proclamation throughout his land calling his people to gather again for battle against the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah and those with him had fled into the wilderness.
Amalickiah took those who went with him into the land of Nephi among the Lamanites.
Amalickiah stirred the Lamanites to anger against the people of Nephi.
The king of the Lamanites sent a proclamation throughout his land calling his people to gather again for battle against the Nephites.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people and the land is unspecified.
The proclamation's medium and means of distribution are unspecified.

narration.text: and did stir up the Lamanites to anger against the people of Nephi,
the king of the Lamanites sent a proclamation throughout all his land, among all his people, that they should gather themselves together again to go to battle against the Nephites.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Use a narration-only retrospective scene; the verse summarizes these events rather than supplying a staged encounter.
Preserve the sequence of Amalickiah's actions and the resulting proclamation without depicting separate times as one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not dramatize the reported events as a new present-tense encounter.
Do not invent words spoken by Amalickiah or the king.
Do not depict the king as physically present with Amalickiah.
Do not show a battle beginning or the commanded gathering as already accomplished.
Do not invent messengers, proclamation readings, or a written document.

title: The people refuse the call
summary: Many Lamanites fear both displeasing the king and going to battle, and do not obey. The king gives Amalickiah command of the obedient part of the army and orders him to compel the others to arms.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites were afraid and most did not obey the king's command to go to battle.
The angry king gave Amalickiah command of the obedient part of his army and ordered him to compel the others to arms.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A divided response among the gathered people may be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where the proclamation was heard and the people's appearance.

narration.text: they would not, or the more part of them would not, obey

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or a specific confrontation between the king and his people.

title: Amalickiah's design
summary: Amalickiah secretly desires to dethrone the Lamanite king.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah desired to dethrone the king of the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amalickiah may be shown alone, visually conveying private thought without adding a specific plan.
unspecified_visual_details: Amalickiah's expression, surroundings, and any physical tokens of his intentions.

narration.text: he laid the plan in his heart to dethrone the king

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific plotting conversation, object, or act not stated in the verse.

title: The Lamanites flee to Onidah
summary: Lamanites who had refused the king's command flee to Onidah, believing the approaching army will destroy them. They appoint a man as king and leader, determined not to be forced to fight the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: The disobedient Lamanites fled to Onidah when they saw the army coming, supposing it intended to destroy them.
They appointed a man king and leader, resolved not to be subjected to fighting the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The refugees may be shown gathered at Onidah with an approaching army visible at a distance.
unspecified_visual_details: The appointed leader's identity and appearance, and the appearance of Onidah.

narration.text: they fled to Onidah, to the place of arms

prohibited_inventions: Do not give the appointed leader a name or imply that he is Lehonti.

title: Gathered on Mount Antipas
summary: The Lamanites gather atop Mount Antipas in preparation for battle. Amalickiah does not intend to fight them; he intends to win their favor, lead them, and seize the kingdom. His army camps in the nearby valley.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites gathered on Mount Antipas in preparation for battle.
Amalickiah intended to gain favor with the Lamanite armies, place himself at their head, dethrone the king, and take the kingdom, rather than give battle.
Amalickiah's army pitched tents in the valley near Mount Antipas.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The mountain and nearby valley can be shown together to clarify their relative locations.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and design of tents and the terrain's exact appearance.

narration.text: he caused his army to pitch their tents

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle between the armies.

title: The first messages to Lehonti
summary: At night Amalickiah sends a secret messenger to Lehonti, asking him to come down from Mount Antipas. Lehonti refuses three successive requests.

explicit_facts.text: At night Amalickiah sent a secret embassy asking Lehonti to come to the foot of Mount Antipas.
Lehonti did not come down despite repeated requests, including three requests described in the account.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A messenger can be shown carrying a message between Amalickiah's camp and Lehonti's position.
unspecified_visual_details: The messenger's identity, appearance, and the precise route taken.

narration.text: he sent a secret embassy into the mount Antipas

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the wording of the messages or show Lehonti descending.

title: Amalickiah climbs the mountain
summary: After failing to persuade Lehonti to come down, Amalickiah climbs nearly to Lehonti's camp and sends a fourth message, asking Lehonti to come down with his guards.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah went up the mountain nearly to Lehonti's camp and sent a fourth message asking Lehonti to come down with his guards.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amalickiah may be shown partway up the mountain, with Lehonti's camp nearby.
unspecified_visual_details: The camp's design, the messenger's identity, and the exact distance between the men.

narration.text: he went up into the mount, nearly to Lehonti’s camp

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lehonti coming down in this scene; that occurs in the next stated event.

title: The secret agreement
summary: Lehonti comes down with his guards to Amalickiah. Amalickiah proposes that Lehonti bring his army down at night to surround Amalickiah's men, promising to deliver them into Lehonti's hands if Amalickiah is made second leader of the whole army.

explicit_facts.text: Lehonti came down with his guards to Amalickiah.
Amalickiah asked Lehonti to surround Amalickiah's camp at night and offered to deliver his men if made second leader of the whole army.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two leaders may be shown conferring with Lehonti's guards present.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact meeting place and the words used in their conversation.

narration.text: if he would make him (Amalickiah) a second leader over the whole army

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue for the proposal.

title: Amalickiah's men are surrounded
summary: Lehonti came down with his men and surrounded Amalickiah's men before they awoke at dawn. When the men saw they were surrounded, they pleaded with Amalickiah to let them join their brethren so they would not be destroyed. This was what Amalickiah desired.

explicit_facts.text: Lehonti came down with his men and surrounded Amalickiah's men before they awoke at dawn.
When Amalickiah's men saw they were surrounded, they pleaded with him to let them join their brethren so they would not be destroyed.
This was what Amalickiah desired.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The surrounding men may be shown in the dim light preceding dawn.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, terrain, number of men, and their clothing and equipment are not specified.

narration.text: Lehonti came down with his men and surrounded the men of Amalickiah,
they plead with Amalickiah that he would suffer them to fall in with their brethren, that they might not be destroyed.
Now this was the very thing which Amalickiah desired.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The plea is reported rather than quoted as direct speech; retain it as narration.
The encirclement precedes the men's awakening and recognition of their situation; do not depict these as simultaneous events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict combat or destruction.
Do not place the scene at a named location not supplied by these verses.
Do not invent direct dialogue for the pleading men.
Do not depict permission being granted or the men joining their brethren; neither occurs in the supplied verses.

title: Amalickiah delivers his men
summary: Amalickiah delivers his men contrary to the king's command. The account explains the Lamanite custom of appointing the second leader as chief leader if the chief is killed.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah delivered his men, contrary to the king's commands, to accomplish his design of dethroning the king.
Among the Lamanites, if the chief leader was killed, the second leader was customarily appointed chief leader.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The delivery may be depicted as Amalickiah's men joining Lehonti's forces.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the custom is shown visually or only conveyed through narration.

narration.text: if their chief leader was killed, to appoint the second leader

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 17 states a custom; it does not narrate a killing in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a leader being killed in this scene.

title: Lehonti dies
summary: Amalickiah has one of his servants administer poison to Lehonti gradually, and Lehonti dies. The Lamanites appoint Amalickiah their leader and chief commander.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah caused one of his servants to administer poison by degrees to Lehonti, who died.
After Lehonti's death, the Lamanites appointed Amalickiah their leader and chief commander.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehonti may be shown weakened as the poison takes effect, without depicting a specific unmentioned method or symptom.
unspecified_visual_details: Where the poisoning and appointment occur, and the poison's appearance or effects.

narration.text: that he died

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the poison being administered in a particular form or invent symptoms.

title: Amalickiah marches to the city
summary: Amalickiah marches with his armies to the city of Nephi. The king comes out with his guards to meet him, believing Amalickiah has obeyed his command and gathered an army against the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah marched with his armies to the land of Nephi and its chief city, the city of Nephi.
The king came out with his guards to meet Amalickiah, believing he had fulfilled the king's commands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two parties may be shown approaching one another outside the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's appearance and the size or arrangement of the forces.

narration.text: the king came out to meet him with his guards

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the king aware of Amalickiah's plot.

title: The king's servants approach
summary: As the king approaches, Amalickiah sends his servants to meet him. They bow as though reverencing him. The king extends his hand to raise the first servant, following a Lamanite custom that signifies peace.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah's servants went to meet the king and bowed as if reverencing him.
The king extended his hand to raise the first servant, a customary token of peace among the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The first servant may be shown bowed before the king as the king reaches down to raise him.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise ceremonial gestures and clothing.

narration.text: as a token of peace

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the stabbing until the next scene.

title: The king is stabbed
summary: The first person raised from the ground stabs the king, who falls. The king's servants flee. Amalickiah's servants cry out, accusing the king's servants of stabbing him.
characters: The first person raised from the ground

explicit_facts.text: The first person raised from the ground stabbed the king to the heart, and the king fell.
The king's servants fled.
Amalickiah's servants cried out and accused the king's servants of stabbing the king.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The stabbing can be shown at the moment it happens without visible injury detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and surroundings.

title: Amalickiah turns the army against the servants
summary: Amalickiah's armies come to the spot and find the king fallen. Pretending to be angry, Amalickiah orders those who loved the king to pursue the king's servants, and they do so.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah's armies found the king lying where he had fallen.
Amalickiah pretended to be angry and ordered those who loved the king to pursue his servants; they pursued.

unspecified_visual_details: The precise route and distance of the pursuit.

title: The king's servants escape
summary: The king's servants flee from the pursuing army into the wilderness, cross into the land of Zarahemla, and join the people of Ammon. The pursuing army returns without catching them, and Amalickiah gains the people's hearts by fraud.

explicit_facts.text: The king's servants fled into the wilderness, crossed into the land of Zarahemla, and joined the people of Ammon.
The pursuing army returned without catching them, and Amalickiah gained the people's hearts by fraud.

title: Amalickiah takes the city

title: The queen sends for Amalickiah
summary: After hearing that the king was slain and that the king's servants escaped, the queen sends to Amalickiah. She asks him to spare the city's people, come to her, and bring witnesses concerning the king's death.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah sent an embassy to the queen telling her that the king had been slain by his servants and that they had escaped pursuit.
The queen asked Amalickiah to spare the city's people, come to her, and bring witnesses concerning the king's death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The queen may be shown receiving the report and sending a messenger with her request.

locations: The queen's audience place in the city of Nephi
